newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity surges on NW cold, natgas rise.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity surges on NW cold, natgas rise.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures settled sharply higher Tuesday, soaring amid cold weather in the Pacific Northwest and a meteoric rise in domestic natural gas prices.
"Everything is driven off Northwest gas prices," said a Houston trader.
Spot natgas prices at the Sumas Hub--the western Canadian export point to the Northwest--were assessed at $3.00-$3.05 per million British thermal units, sharply higher than $2.22-$2.27 on Monday.
Down at the southern California border, swing natural gas was quoted in the mid- to high-$2.90s per million British thermal units, up more than 20 cents from Monday.
Heating demand jumped in the Northwest when heavy rain and snow hit the region late Monday.
Higher power usage combined with tighter electricity supplies due to several power plant outages in the West also bolstered spot cash prices, market sources said.

In the Northwest, the 700 megawatt (MW) unit 4 at the Colstrip coal-fired station was scheduled to restart Thursday, while the 550 MW unit 3 at the Jim Bridger plant in Wyoming was said to be expected for restart today.

In the Southwest, the 790 MW unit 1 at the Mohave coal-fired complex near Laughlin, Nev., is expected to be back up Wednesday, while unit 3 at the Four Corners coal-fired plant in Arizona was expected to resume operation today.
The 360 MW unit 1 at the Springerville, Ariz., facility was scheduled to return to full output some time Tuesday.
Moreover, Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) today raised next-day power prices for delivery in the Northwest by $1.75 a megawatt hour (MWh) following a $1.50 increase Monday.
December California-Oregon Border (COB) futures settled at a new life-of-contract high of $27.25, a dollar above its previous high of $26.25 recorded on Monday.
January COB finished up cents at $23.67 after peaking at $24.00 today. Most deferred COB ended 10 to 70 cents higher.
December Palo Verde (PV) futures posted a new contract high at $25.75, surpassing a previous high of $25.60. The spot contract settled the day at $25.42, up $1.42.
January PV finished up $1.07 at $22.40, shaving a $1.67 gain. Outer PV months were mostly inactive, but ended 20 cents to $1.10 above Monday's settlement.
NYMEX estimated 388 COB and 128 PV contracts were sold today.
